name: Black Eyes
label: Dischord
lede: Two drummers facing each other, two bassists, one guitarist in the middle: three years, two albums, a split before the second one came out, and a comeback record twenty-one years later.

eras.title: Symmetry and noise
eras.text: Out of the house-show bands Trooper and the No-Gos came a five-piece built like a mirror. Dischord's bio describes the stage: a drummer on each side, a bassist front and back, the guitarist dead center, and shows that turned into chaotic, rhythmic jams the crowd joined in on.

years.p: [[Daniel Martin-McCormick|54e187d1-c4f3-4b5b-8eeb-e592a5573a29]], Hugh McElroy, Jacob Long, [[Dan Caldas|da0d355e-28bb-476b-8dbb-173e1899d097]] and [[Mike Kanin|a3234fdc-aa51-47af-986b-cc75c30f8a6d]] start playing as Black Eyes. Most had already played together in Trooper and [[The No-Gos|15e434f9-fd72-4a37-9ced-0e65724f3302]].
years.xp:
The line-up: Daniel Martin-McCormick on guitar, Hugh McElroy on bass, Jacob Long on bass and guitar, and Dan Caldas and Mike Kanin on drums. McElroy and Martin-McCormick shared lead vocals, one of the band's signatures.

Two full kits meant the rhythm section could lock together or pull apart, and the band leaned into both.

years.h: Black Eyes' Some Boys / Shut Up, I Never · Ruffian Records
years.p: A two-song 7" on Ruffian, the DIY label Hugh McElroy ran.
On Planaria Recordings, with the Black Eyes song Have Been Murdered Again.

eras.title: Gone before Cough
eras.text: Ian MacKaye produced the debut, and a long run on the road with Q and Not U took the band across the country. Then, with a second album finished and a saxophone added, they quit.

years.h: Black Eyes' self-titled debut · Dischord No. 135
years.p: Produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], recorded by [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]. Dual vocals, two full drum kits, and flashes of horn and synth over post-hardcore that wanted to dance.

years.h: On the road with [[Q and Not U|a934e33f-b3cb-47dd-9638-f7f1f25fe162]]
years.p: Black Eyes tour extensively with their Dischord labelmates, the last big push before the end.

years.h: Black Eyes' last show, at the Black Cat
years.p: Black Eyes play their final show at the Black Cat and break up, two months before their second album, Cough, is due.

Released after the band had already split. Jacob Long had moved to saxophone, and the record leans hard into improvisation and dub; Wikipedia's summary calls it frenzied brass pushing into free-jazz territory.

eras.title: Scattered to dub and drone
eras.text: For eighteen years the members went into electronic music, drone, noise and record-making, often with each other. Nobody played a Black Eyes song in public until 2023.

years.h: After Black Eyes: Earthen Sea, Mi Ami, Marriage, Ruffian
years.p: Jacob Long makes electronic music as [[Earthen Sea|5dbcb05c-6cfd-4fcf-a803-daaac08d328a]], Daniel Martin-McCormick plays in Marriage and [[Mi Ami|0e7ef08c-e735-48f9-a07c-cff6b546c978]], and Hugh McElroy keeps Ruffian going and produces [[Priests|e708ace7-5c5e-48dd-be9b-c5c3aed6273b]].
years.xp: Mike Kanin later started the On Repeat imprint at Astral Spirits.

eras.title: Not a nostalgia trip
eras.text: The reunion was meant to be a few anniversary shows of old songs. It turned into new writing, a festival named after the band's own history, and the first Black Eyes album in twenty-one years, still on Dischord and still produced by MacKaye.

years.h: Black Eyes' debut reissued, with demos and a zine history
years.p: Black Eyes returns with unreleased demos and live sets, plus Speaking In Tongues: Black Eyes 2001–2004, a 48-page zine history of the band and the DC scene around it.

q: We only played old material and it was really exciting.
years.h: Black Eyes reunite: first shows in nineteen years
years.p: In November 2022 Black Eyes announced a reunion for their debut's 20th anniversary. They played three shows of old material in April 2023, and by July were writing again.
years.xp: Hugh McElroy told Treble the first plan was just to play the old songs, with no guarantee it would work. New ideas were traded remotely, with Mike Kanin sending them from Austin, but didn't come together until all five were in one room.

years.h: Reunion full set at the Black Cat, April 7, 2023
yt: Reunion full set at the Black Cat, April 7, 2023

years.p: Cough, released after the 2004 breakup, gets a 20th-anniversary reissue as Black Eyes keep touring and road-testing new songs.

years.h: Black Eyes' Speaking in Tongues festival
years.p: A four-day festival named after the band's 2023 archival zine, Speaking In Tongues, per Treble.

q: We tracked and mostly mixed it in three days.
years.p: Six new songs recorded at Tonal Park with MacKaye producing and Don Godwin engineering. Same two drums, bass, guitar and sax as Cough, now with live multichannel dubbing, drum triggers, samples and some bass clarinet.
years.xp: The first Black Eyes album in more than two decades was cut fast. Daniel Martin-McCormick told Treble they tracked and mostly mixed it in three days.
